key_insight: Aggregate scores can hide weaknesses in next-visit diagnosis prediction; LONGINUS combines retrieval and memory to improve performance across diagnosis transitions.
clinical_relevance: Distinguishing persistent, newly recorded, and recurrent diagnoses may make evaluation more informative, but the study does not establish clinical benefit.
method: Evaluate diagnosis-set size, long-tailed labels, temporal transitions, and observed history depth.
Combine evidence retrieved from patient records with structured memory of the patient trajectory.
Preserve predictions shared by both views and adjudicate disagreements without revealing their source.
evidence_signal: Across MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV with four LLM backbones, LONGINUS led LLM-based methods on transition-specific performance in nearly all settings, while repeating the last visit outperformed most LLM approaches overall.
watch_item: Cross-view agreement is a reliability heuristic, not proof of correctness; prospective validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication
